content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposed an incremental learning method by introducing a "LongShortTerm Strategy." By building a short term learner branch, the strategy can train a balanced model to solve the "long short term dilemma." It is an ideal and effective strategy to solve the dilemma.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:  This strategy is undoubtedly novel and reasonable, and in combination with this strategy, the authors propose some data enhancements and design of loss function to give the method better results. 

Weakness: However, there are some concerns. 1. The name of the strategy, "LongShortTerm Strategy," may be reconsidered. On the one hand, the name of it reminds me of Long Short Term Memory (LSTM), which tends to give the wrong guidance. 2. The writing in the methods section is somewhat confusing, making it difficult to understand the major parts of the work and the innovations. 3. Following comment 2. The idea is excellent but attractive work is not found. 4. I can not get what is the "long term learner M(T)(i-1)"  in the description of Figure 2.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The article is generally well-written, but the method section is slightly confusing. There is no doubt that idea proposed in this article is very original and in inovative.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, this paper is innovative. The proposed "LongShortTerm Strategy" has good potential, but the method is not very attractive at the present version.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper introduces a novel incremental learning algorithm to mitigate the trade-off between long and short-term learning. The authors also analyse the effects of data augmentation over these learning processes and propose Margin-based Data Augmentation (MDA) for adjustable data augmentation. They test their model on the ImageNet-100 and ImageNet-1K datasets and claim to achieve state-of-the-art results in comparison with related methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Main Weaknesses:
- The paper needs proofreading. Several sentences are not well written (e.g. "knowledge more or less",  "is exclusive each other", etc.), all the citations need an adjustment in their formatting, and some are ill-located (e.g. last phrase of the first paragraph). 
- It is not completely clear why the dubbed “long short term dilemma”, that the authors claim to have discovered, is fundamentally different from the well-known forgetting phenomena.
- In Sec. 3.1 the authors describe the employed metrics but do not provide references.
- The proposed MDA is not contrasted with the existing literature.

Main Strengths:
- The paper achieves state-of-the-art results on the incremental learning problem.
- The authors propose new methodologies for incremental learning and data augmentation.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is mostly clear. The authors propose a new methodology. The new algorithms are provided in the main text, probably allowing reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: Although the paper needs proofreading, it is mostly clear and organized. The authors propose novel approaches for incremental learning and data augmentation, achieving state-of-the-art results. My main concern is that they claim to have discovered the “long short term dilemma”, which I believe is fundamentally the forgetting problem. Therefore I am not totally confident to recommend acceptance, and therefore I would like to see the comments of the fellow reviewers about this point.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper investigates the continual learning problem and suggests a mismatch between the solution that is optimal for the new task and the one that is more transferable (i.e., brings better performance at long term).  The assumptions are centred around data augmentations, stronger data augmentation are more transferable (of buffer samples) but might be more constraining for the task being learned. 
Based on this, the authors suggest a solution with two models, at the beginning of each task, they are initialized from the same model, one is trained with heavy memory augmentation (long term branch) and the other is trained with softer augmentation (short term).
Experiments on ImageNet show improvements over existing works. The authors perform some empirical analysis that supports their assumption.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
1) New observation related to a different performance w.r.t to the casted augmentations between recent task performance and long term performance. 
2) Simple solution.
3) Good results.
Weakness:
1) The whole long short term dilemma is quite interesting but it is a bit disappointing that is only explained  w.r.t data augmentations usage for vision transformers.
2) Experiments are conducted on only ImageNet dataset with only Vision Transformers as a base model. Does the same observation extends to ResNet? Data augmentations are not specific to transformers.
3) Important baselines are missing: the performance of the model with heavy augmentations, and that with softer augmentations.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
While the paper is in general easy to follow, some points are unclear:
1. In Fig.1, it is unclear what measure of performance is used and w.r.t to which tasks.
2. The introduced metric doesn't make much sense for incremental classification, i.e., the normalization by number of classes, with incremental classification one can just use the overall acc. It seems that the metric is only introduces for the purpose of the proposed solution.
3. It is not quite clear whether augmentations strategies is applied only to the buffer samples or to both new and memory data.
4. There is no ablation on the buffer size.
5. It is unclear how the magnitude of augmentation is set.
6. What does step.4 in Alg.1 mean?
7.The last two sentences of section 4.1 are unclear to me.
8. Differences in table 2 are not that significant. 
9. The first sentence of section 4.5 is not clear not supported.
content.summary_of_the_review: While the paper brings what might seem to be an interesting observation, the long short term dilemma, the reasoning is limited to data augmentations and to vision transformers which is limiting the impact of this work. Limited experiments are performed and some parts are not quite clear.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper: (1) studies the "long short term dilemma"; (2) proposes a multi-branch architecture where a branch focuses on the immediate task and the other focuses on future tasks; and (3) adjusts the data augmentation strategy for each branch to optimise for short term (current task) and long term (future tasks). Experiments are conducted using ViT on ImageNet-100 and ImageNet-1K and compared with other methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Weakness:
- The "long short term dilemma" is already well-known from prior work as the stability-plasticity dilemma [French, 1997; Mermillod et al., 2013].
- The multi-branch architecture is in essence an architecture approach that expands the capacity of the model whereas all baseline models are regularisation/replay/distillation approaches. No mention or analysis of the computational demands this method requires in comparison with existing work.
-  No theoretical or intuitive justification is provided to explain why does data augmentation play a role in the "long short term dilemma"?
- All baselines but one use a weaker CNN model whereas the proposed method uses a much more powerful ViT model voiding any fair comparison.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarify: The paper is clear.
Quality: There are numerous language errors in the paper.
Novelty: The paper presents no novel insights.
Reproducibility: All details to reproduce the work are provided.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper presents several empirical observations on a narrow class of models and datasets but none of the contributions of the paper are novel.
content.correctness: 1: The main claims of the paper are incorrect or not at all supported by theory or empirical results.
